items.title: Same duty cycle, very different outcomes: What tough materials taught us about histotripsy
items.text: One of the questions that stayed with me throughout my Ph.D. was surprisingly simple: Why are some tissues so much harder to break down with histotripsy than others? Histotripsy is a focused ultrasound technique that uses cavitation bubbles to mechanically break down tissue. Unlike thermal ablation, the goal is not to heat the tissue. Instead, the rapid activity of these bubbles creates mechanical stresses that progressively disrupt tissue structure.

items.title: Choline supplementation in young children with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder can have durable developmental benefits
items.text: Children affected by prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) experience long-lasting cognitive gains after treatment with supplemental choline, an essential nutrient, a new study suggests. The findings point to a potentially scalable intervention for neurodevelopmental differences that currently have few treatment options. Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) is an umbrella term for several diagnoses that affect 1%–5% of the global population and can involve physical, cognitive and behavioral deficits and challenges.

items.title: Changes in marital status may heighten vulnerability for alcohol-related problems
items.text: People who have experienced mixed marital transitions or who have never been married may be more likely to have alcohol-related problems than people with stable marital status. According to a study published in Alcohol: Clinical and Experimental Research, people in early midlife who have experienced mixed marital transitions and individuals who remain never married into late life are particularly vulnerable to alcohol use problems. The study highlights the connections between romantic relationships and alcohol use and the need for further evaluation of interventions tailored to age, sex and life stage to reduce the risk of problematic alcohol use for people going through marital transitions.

items.title: Is ADHD on the rise in children and adults in the U.K. and Europe?
items.text: ADHD seems to be in the news everywhere, but is this due to a rise in cases or to changing awareness and diagnosis? Pulling together the evidence for a presentation to Europe's main clinical neuroscience conference, Professor Anita Thapar said, "The rise in cases of ADHD across Europe appears mainly due to a change in awareness and diagnosis. Indeed, there is growing evidence that ADHD is still underdiagnosed in some countries."

items.title: Menopause is marked by a body-wide physiological 'cliff,' study suggests
items.text: The final menstrual period is preceded by abrupt "cliff-like" biological changes across multiple body systems, some of which show early signs more than a decade beforehand, according to research published in Nature Medicine. The findings suggest that menopause-related physiological changes may occur over a shorter time frame than previously thought and advance our understanding of how early these changes can be detected.
